sections.heading: C2 — Impaired, distracted and drowsy driving
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Impaired, distracted and drowsy driving

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A06
The underage possession-and-consumption subsection excludes alcohol connected with a religious service or alcohol possessed or consumed by members of the same family in a family member’s private home. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A06
At a DUI arrest, the officer confiscates the driver license except for an out-of-state license holder and issues a 15-day temporary license. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A06
A DUI-arrested driver has 15 days to request an administrative hearing; without a request, the license is revoked when that period ends. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A06
An eligible temporary license may be extended when the administrative hearing is requested. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A06
An administrative DUI hearing examines the officer’s probable cause, the evidence of impaired driving or control, and refusal after warning about revocation. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A06
An unfavorable probable-cause hearing ruling brings a three-month revocation for a first offense. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A06
An unfavorable probable-cause hearing ruling brings a 12-month revocation for a second offense. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A06
An unfavorable probable-cause hearing ruling brings an 18-month revocation for a third or later offense. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A06
An unfavorable chemical-refusal hearing ruling brings a 12-month revocation for a first offense. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A06
An unfavorable chemical-refusal hearing ruling brings an 18-month revocation for a second offense. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A06
An unfavorable chemical-refusal hearing ruling brings a 24-month revocation for a third or later offense. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A07
Reinstatement after a probable-cause or chemical-refusal revocation requires the designated alcohol-evaluation course or rehabilitation, payment of related fees, service of the revocation period and a $200 reinstatement fee. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A07
Vision, knowledge and road-skills testing may be required before reinstatement following probable-cause or chemical-refusal action. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A07
The first-DUI-offense table assigns 12 months of license loss for drugs or BAC below 0.15. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A07
The first-DUI-offense table assigns 18 months of license loss for the BAC bracket labeled 0.15 through 0.19. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A07
The first-DUI-offense table assigns 24 months of license loss for BAC at least 0.20 or chemical-test refusal. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A07
For a first DUI offense, the court-sanctions table lists a $500 to $1,500 fine, imprisonment up to 12 months, or both. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A07
A person entering First Offender Election instead of trial may seek an IID license before the revocation period ends. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R19 | anchor: A07
For FOE violations dated February 2, 2015 or later, immediate IID application eligibility remains subject to the program’s listed requirements. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R20 | anchor: A07
The FOE IID application requires surrender of the Delaware license, a completed application, proof of insurance and Delaware vehicle registration, and no other withdrawal that prevents IID licensing. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R21 | anchor: A07
After FOE IID requirements are met, the DMV authorizes device installation on the approved vehicles. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R22 | anchor: A07
A FOE participant with an IID license must remain in the IID program for four months starting on the IID license issue date. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R23 | anchor: A07
FOE reinstatement requires DMV receipt of satisfactory alcohol-program completion and a $200 fee; vision, law and road tests may also be required before DMV authorizes IID removal. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R24 | anchor: A08
A FOE participant without a vehicle in their name who chooses no IID license must serve the full revocation, refrain from driving and meet the remaining reinstatement requirements. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R25 | anchor: A08
The second-DUI-offense table assigns 18 months of license loss for drugs or BAC below 0.15. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R26 | anchor: A08
The second-DUI-offense table assigns 24 months of license loss for the BAC bracket labeled 0.15 through 0.19. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R27 | anchor: A08
The second-DUI-offense table assigns 30 months of license loss for BAC at least 0.20 or chemical-test refusal. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R28 | anchor: A08
The second-DUI-offense court table lists a $750 to $2,500 fine and imprisonment from 60 days to 18 months. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R29 | anchor: A08
For an eligible second-DUI offender, the court may suspend the minimum prison term after successful participation in its Court of Common Pleas DUI Treatment Program. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R30 | anchor: A08
The third-DUI-offense table assigns 24 months of license loss for drugs or BAC below 0.15. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R31 | anchor: A08
The third-DUI-offense table assigns 30 months of license loss for the BAC bracket labeled 0.15 through 0.19. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R32 | anchor: A08
The third-DUI-offense table assigns 36 months of license loss for BAC at least 0.20 or chemical-test refusal. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R33 | anchor: A08
A third DUI offense committed at any time after two prior offenses is classified as a Class G felony. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R34 | anchor: A08
The third-DUI-offense court table lists a fine up to $5,000. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R35 | anchor: A08
The third-DUI-offense court table lists imprisonment from one to two years. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R36 | anchor: A08
A fourth DUI offense committed at any time after three prior offenses is classified as a Class E felony. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

sections.heading: C2 — Impaired, distracted and drowsy driving
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Impaired, distracted and drowsy driving — continuation

FACT_ID: sec06-R37 | anchor: A08
Every fourth-DUI-offense conviction carries 60 months of license loss in the DMV table. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R38 | anchor: A08
The fourth-DUI-offense court table lists a fine up to $7,000. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R39 | anchor: A08
The fourth-DUI-offense court table lists imprisonment from two to five years. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R40 | anchor: A08
A fifth DUI offense is classified as a Class E felony. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R41 | anchor: A08
Every fifth-DUI-offense conviction carries 60 months of license loss in the DMV table. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R42 | anchor: A08
The fifth-DUI-offense court table lists a fine up to $10,000. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R43 | anchor: A08
The fifth-DUI-offense court table lists imprisonment from three to five years. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R44 | anchor: A09
A sixth DUI offense is classified as a Class D felony. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R45 | anchor: A09
Every sixth-DUI-offense conviction carries 60 months of license loss in the DMV table. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R46 | anchor: A09
The sixth-DUI-offense court table lists a fine up to $10,000. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R47 | anchor: A09
The sixth-DUI-offense court table lists imprisonment from four to eight years. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R48 | anchor: A09
A seventh or later DUI offense is classified as a Class C felony. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R49 | anchor: A09
Every seventh-or-later DUI conviction carries 60 months of license loss in the DMV table. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R50 | anchor: A09
The seventh-or-later DUI court table lists a fine up to $15,000. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R51 | anchor: A09
The seventh-or-later DUI court table lists imprisonment from five to 15 years. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R52 | anchor: A09
An IID license permits operation of an IID-equipped vehicle only after the participant meets all minimum qualifications. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R53 | anchor: A09
FOE participants are immediately eligible to apply for an IID license when entering the program, subject to its other qualifications. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R54 | anchor: A09
For a non-FOE first conviction, the IID table gives a minimum revocation of 30 to 45 days before application eligibility, depending on BAC. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R55 | anchor: A09
For a second conviction, the IID table gives a 60-day minimum revocation before application eligibility, subject to other qualifications. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R56 | anchor: A09
For a third conviction, the IID table gives a 90-day minimum revocation before application eligibility, subject to other qualifications. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R57 | anchor: A09
For a fourth or later conviction, the IID table gives a six-month minimum revocation before application eligibility, subject to other qualifications. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R58 | anchor: A09
An IID license cannot be used for CDL-class vehicles or peripheral endorsements, and the qualifying offense must not involve death or serious injury. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R59 | anchor: A09
Other suspensions, revocations, disqualifications, denials or statutory disqualification criteria can prevent issuance of an IID license. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R60 | anchor: A09
The general IID application process requires a valid Delaware license at the time of the offense, an application, the required treatment enrollment and fees, and surrender of the currently issued Delaware license. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R61 | anchor: A09
An IID applicant must provide insurance proof for the vehicles on which devices will be installed. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R62 | anchor: A10
The IID process requires proof of valid Delaware registration and installation on every vehicle the participant will operate during revocation, even a vehicle the participant does not own. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R63 | anchor: A10
Vision, knowledge and road-skills testing may be required before an IID license is issued. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R64 | anchor: A10
After all IID conditions are met, the DMV authorizes an approved vendor’s installation and verifies installation before issuing limited driving privileges for the approved vehicles. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R65 | anchor: A10
The IID participant pays all program costs and must keep devices installed for the required period, measured from IID license issuance rather than the original revocation end date. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R66 | anchor: A10
The IID duration table requires four months for a FOE participant. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R67 | anchor: A10
For a non-FOE first conviction, the IID duration table requires 12 to 23 months, depending on BAC. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R68 | anchor: A10
For a second conviction, the IID duration table requires 16 to 28 months, depending on BAC. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R69 | anchor: A10
For a third conviction, the IID duration table requires 21 to 33 months, depending on BAC. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R70 | anchor: A10
The IID duration table requires at least 54 months for a fourth or later conviction. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R71 | anchor: A10
Noncompliance can cause the DMV to extend IID time or disqualify the participant. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R72 | anchor: A10
A DUI offender who does not apply for the IID program must serve the entire revocation and cannot drive during it. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0059]
